Eva —

Thanks for the clear list. We can absolutely provide all requested artifacts. Short summary and items attached / linked below so your team can start review while we assemble any remaining exports: 

1) EU-only processing: Redwood supports region-restriction policies at the tenant level. When you opt into "EU-only processing" we pin compute and storage to our Frankfurt (eu-central) and Amsterdam (eu-west) clusters and apply routing rules to avoid non-EU fallbacks. I confirm in writing: with the regional residency toggle enabled there will be no intentional routing of ClinicX traffic to non-EU regions.

2) VPC architecture: attached is a network-architecture-eu-vpc.png that shows our private connector (customer egress), optional private control-plane peering, and how KV cache and logs are handled. Note: the control plane performs orchestration metadata operations but is designed not to persist customer input when the "private deployment" option is chosen.

3) Compliance docs: attached is a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and a CAIQ/SIG export (see "redwood-sccs-annex.pdf" which contains our SCC/AIA references and the CAIQ summary).

4) DPIA note: we've prepared a short DPIA summary tailored to ClinicX concerns (attached as dpia-summary-clinicx-20261123.docx). It highlights transfer risk mitigation (SCCs + contractual assurances + customer-managed KMS) and residual risk scoring.

Open items: if you need executed SCCs/ANNEX signatures, we typically provide the standard SCC addendum and can route a DocuSign link (please confirm signatory). Also, if ClinicX requires an on-premises private control-plane appliance (air-gapped), that's handled by our Private deployment track and would be a separate procurement item.

I've looped in Marissa for commercial follow-up and Laura from CS to coordinate any technical walkthroughs.

Next steps: I'll upload the files to a GDrive folder and share links, and can schedule a technical call tomorrow to walk the DPIA and architecture.

Best,
Soojin Lee

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: ClinicX — control plane retention and SCC question

Looping in quick technical clarifications for the DPA/SCC answer. See my notes below (will paste into a reply to ClinicX):

- Telemetry/trace retention toggle: tenant-level boolean "enable_customer_telemetry" (default true for Hosted). When set to false (UI/API), all request-level telemetry, traces, and sampled logs are suppressed. Stored KV cache and customer artifacts continue to be pinned to the selected region; operational logs required for billing/uptime are retained for 30 days and purged unless longer retention is contractually required (we mark this as 30d in our DPA table).
- Control-plane persistence: for "Redwood Private (VPC)" customers the control plane may run in a customer-managed VPC; in that configuration we run a reduced control-plane that does not capture raw prompts. For Hosted customers that require EU-only routing, the control-plane still manages routing but we provide an optional privacy config.
- SCC/DPA posture: our standard DPA includes the SCC clauses as an Annex. Customers can either sign the full DPA (recommended) or append a limited Annex that scopes processing to platform operations only; legal must approve the limited scope. For procurement speed, many EU customers sign the full DPA + SCC Annex; we can provide a draft marked-up for ClinicX.

Recommend Soojin send an explicit single-paragraph answer to the two questions and attach the DPA draft for their counsel.

Rishi
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Eva / ClinicX team —

Short answers to your two outstanding points: 

1) Telemetry/Retention toggle: set tenant configuration parameter "enable_customer_telemetry" = false. When set to false: request-level telemetry, sampled traces, and user-input logging are disabled; billing and operational metrics at aggregate levels remain for 30 days. We have attached a screenshot of the admin UI showing the toggle and a short excerpt from our config guide.

2) SCCs / DPA approach: Redwood's standard path is the full DPA which includes SCC Annex A (data exporter/processor clauses). If ClinicX prefers a more limited annex that only covers platform routing and ephemeral cache behavior, legal can prepare a scoped annex but this requires review and is subject to redlines. For procurement velocity we recommend executing the standard DPA + SCC Annex; attached is a draft DPA for your counsel to review.
